newsitem.title: IRAQ: Saddam assails U.S. over embassy in Israel.
newsitem.headline: Saddam assails U.S. over embassy in Israel.

text.p: Iraqi leader Saddam Hussein assailed the United States over a vote by its House of Representatives reaffirming an earlier commitment to move the U.S. embassy in Israel to Jerusalem by 1999, Baghdad radio reported on Sunday.

"...The timing and nature of this decision proves that America regards those who believes that it is playing a balanced role in the Arab-Zionist dispute as nothing but zeros when it comes to Zionist weight," the radio quoted Saddam as saying during a cabinet meeting.
"The Arabs should mobilise their efforts on the basis that America is always with the Zionist entity against the Arabs' interests," he said.
Saddam said he was ready to discuss with Arab rulers "maintaining Arab dignity and national security regardless of the past and its differences and details."
Iraq's former information minister Abdul-al-Ghani Abdul-al- Ghafur condemned the House vote and urged Arab countries to sever ties with Washington.
"The transfer of any embassy to Jerusalem is an act of aggression against the Arabs which is unacceptable," Ghafur said in a commentary published by al-Jumhouriya newspaper.

Ghafur, who is a leading Baath party member, said Arab rulers should stick to a decision taken by the Arab summit held in Amman in 1980 which urged Arab countries to "sever all ties with any state which recognises Jerusalem as capital for Israel or moves its embassy to it."
Iraq, which fired scores of Scud missiles on the Jewish state during the 1991 Gulf War over Kuwait, is still theoretically at war with Israel.
Its official media carried reports opposing the making of peace by Arabs with Israel. Baghdad has also denied Western reports of clandestine contacts with Tel Aviv.
